title: Build a Tetris game as a single static HTML file named `index.html` in the repo ...
statement:
Build a Tetris game as a single static HTML file named `index.html` in the repo root.

Requirements:
- A playfield 10 columns wide and 20 rows tall. Row 0 is the top row.
- The seven tetrominoes: `I`, `O`, `T`, `S`, `Z`, `J`, `L`. Give each one its own colour.
- A piece spawns at the top and falls one row at a time under gravity.
- When a piece can no longer fall, it locks in place and the next piece spawns.
- The player can move the falling piece left and right, soft drop it (one row down), and hard
  drop it. A hard drop sends the piece straight down to the lowest position it can reach and
 ...

title: Build Tetris game in single HTML file
statement: Build a Tetris game as a single static HTML file named `index.html` in the repo root with a 10×20 playfield, seven tetrominoes, gravity-based piece movement, locking, player controls (left, right, soft/hard drop), and score/level/lines display.
acceptance: index.html created in repo root
Playfield 10 columns × 20 rows with data-testid and data-row/data-col attributes
Seven tetrominoes (I, O, T, S, Z, J, L) each with distinct colour via CSS classes
Piece spawns at top and falls one row at a time
Piece locks when it cannot fall further; next piece spawns
Player can move left, right, soft drop (down one row), hard drop (straight to bottom, locks immediately)
Score, level, lines display (initial values: score 0, level 1, lines 0)
Single file with inline CSS and JS, no frameworks or external resources
Works when opened directly from filesystem
DOM updated synchronously after state changes (no requestAnimationFrame deferral)
sub_requirements: Playfield structure and dimensions
All seven tetrominoes defined and coloured
Gravity and piece falling mechanics
Player input handling (movement and drops)
Score/level/lines tracking and display
Line clearing and scoring (not implemented)
Rotation and game-over handling (not implemented)

title: Add rotation, and settle how a piece locks.
statement:
Add rotation, and settle how a piece locks.

- The player can rotate the falling piece clockwise. Add `"rotateCW"` to the actions
  `window.__tetris.input(action)` accepts.
- A rotation must never put the piece outside the board or on top of a locked cell. If the
  rotated shape does not fit where it is, the game may shift it sideways to make room. If
  nothing works, refuse the rotation and leave the piece exactly as it was.

Locking rule — this is a decision, keep it for the rest of the project:
- A gravity step moves the falling piece down one row. If it cannot move down, that step
  counts...

title: Add rotation, and settle how a piece locks
statement: The player can rotate falling pieces clockwise, and a piece locks after delay with movement-based restart rules and a cap on restarts.
acceptance: input("rotateCW") action is accepted and rotates piece clockwise
Up arrow or X key triggers clockwise rotation
Rotation attempts sideways shifts (±1, ±2 columns) if direct rotation does not fit
Rotation is refused if no position fits piece on board
I piece at top of board is moved down just enough to stay on board when rotated
Gravity step that cannot move down increments lock delay tick counter
Piece locks when lock delay reaches 2 ticks
Left or right movement while piece is resting restarts lock delay counter to 0
Lock delay can restart at most 3 times per piece; fourth restart-triggering move does not reset counter
Restart count persists with piece even if it falls further
sub_requirements: Clockwise rotation with wall kicks
Lock delay mechanism with tick counting
Lock delay restart on sideways movement
Lock delay restart cap at 3 per piece

title: Add line clears and scoring.
statement:
Add line clears and scoring.

- When a piece locks, every full row is removed and everything above it drops down.
- Count the rows removed in `lines` and show it.

Scoring model — this is a decision, keep it for the rest of the project:
- Points for a clear depend on how many rows go at once:
  1 row = 100, 2 rows = 300, 3 rows = 500, 4 rows = 800.
- That number is multiplied by the current level.
- Soft drop scores 1 point for each cell the piece moves down under the player's control.
- Hard drop scores 2 points for each cell the piece drops.

The reason for the table: clearing rows together ...

title: Add line clears and scoring
statement: When a piece locks, every full row is removed, everything above drops down, rows cleared are counted, and points are awarded based on rows cleared at once and current level.
acceptance: Full rows are automatically removed when a piece locks

Clear points are multiplied by the current level
Soft drop scores 1 point per cell when player presses down
Hard drop scores 2 points per cell dropped
sub_requirements: Detect and remove full rows when piece locks
Drop rows above cleared rows
Update lines counter
Award clear points based on quantity at once, multiplied by level
Award drop points for soft and hard drop

title: Two additions.
statement:
Two additions.

Next-piece preview:
- Show the next **three** upcoming pieces, soonest first.

Game over:
- When a newly spawned piece has nowhere to go, the game ends.
- `data-testid="game-over"` — shown when the game is over.
- `window.__tetris.getState().status` becomes `"gameover"`.
- Once the game is over, gravity steps ...

statement: Show the next three upcoming pieces with colour coding, and end the game when a newly spawned piece has nowhere to go.
acceptance: Next-piece preview shows three upcoming pieces with data-testid='next-piece' container

title: Players are complaining about the down key.
statement:
Players are complaining about the down key.

"I slam a piece down with the down arrow and it locks under my fingers before I can nudge it.
Tapping left or right at the bottom gives me a moment to think, but tapping down doesn't."

Fix that: a soft drop on a piece that is already resting on the stack should buy the player
the same breathing room a sideways move buys.

title: Fix down key breathing room
statement: A soft drop on a piece that is already resting on the stack should buy the player the same breathing room a sideways move buys.
acceptance: Pressing down on a resting piece resets its lock timer
Down on a resting piece shares the 3 resets per piece limit with left and right
Down on a resting piece scores nothing (piece does not move)
Soft drop on a falling piece continues to score per cell moved
sub_requirements: Reset lock timer when down is pressed on resting piece
Apply same 3-reset limit to down as exists for sideways moves
Maintain scoring behavior (no score for resting piece soft drop)

title: Three upcoming pieces is too much information — it turns the game into a plannin...
statement:
Three upcoming pieces is too much information — it turns the game into a planning exercise and
it crowds the panel. Show only the next piece.

Keep the colour-coding in the preview. That part works.

title: Show only next piece in preview
statement: The preview panel displays only the next piece instead of three upcoming pieces.
acceptance: Preview panel shows only the next piece
Colour-coding in preview is preserved
Game internally maintains 3-piece queue (unchanged from REQ-004)
sub_requirements: Reduce preview display from 3 pieces to 1 piece
Maintain colour-coding of displayed piece
Keep internal queue unchanged

title: Two additions.
statement:
Two additions.

Levels and speed:
- The level starts at 1 and goes up by one for every 10 lines cleared. It never goes down.
- The higher the level, the faster gravity runs. The interval between gravity steps, in
  milliseconds, is `max(100, 1000 - (level - 1) * 100)`.
- `window.__tetris.getState()` gains `dropInterval` — that interval in milliseconds.
- `window.__tetris.tick(n)` is unchanged: it always advances exactly n gravity steps, whatever
  the level is.
- Add `window.__tetris.setLevel(n)` — sets the current level to n, for testing. Levelling from
  lines carries on from there, and the ...

acceptance: Level display updates as lines are cleared past multiples of 10
Gravity timer interval adjusts to dropInterval() based on current level
setLevel(n) sets level and restarts gravity at new speed
Hold action (C, Shift key) stores current piece and swaps with held piece

Piece from hold spawns at spawn position; failure to fit ends game
Hold display renders held piece or empty data-piece
getState() returns dropInterval milliseconds and hold letter/null
sub_requirements: Level starts at 1, increases by 1 per 10 lines cleared, never goes down
Gravity interval formula: max(100, 1000 - (level - 1) * 100) milliseconds
getState() exposes dropInterval and level

title: Bug report from a player:
statement:
Bug report from a player:

"I've been grinding at level 5. I set up a well, dropped an I piece down it and took four rows
at once — and it scored me less than the two-row clears I'd been getting, twice over. Four
rows in one go is the hardest thing in the game. It can't be worth less than doing it the
easy way."

Reproduce it and fix it.

title: Two additions.
statement:
Two additions.

Ghost piece:
- Show where the falling piece would land, as an outline at the bottom of the board.
- Ghost cells carry `data-ghost="true"`. They are not filled cells — leave their
  `data-filled` as `"false"`.
- `window.__tetris.getState()` gains `ghost` — the array of `[row, col]` cells the ghost
  occupies.

Pause:
- `data-testid="pause-btn"` — a button that pauses and resumes.
- `data-testid="paused-indicator"` — shown while the game is paused.
- `window.__tetris.getState().status` becomes `"paused"` while paused.
- Add `"pause"` to the actions `window.__tetris.input(action)`...

acceptance: Ghost cells displayed as outline at bottom of board with data-ghost="true"

sub_requirements: Ghost piece: visual outline and state tracking

title: Final pass.
statement:
Final pass.

Add keyboard controls:
- Left and Right arrows move the piece.
- Down arrow soft drops.
- Up arrow rotates clockwise.
- Space hard drops.
- C holds.
- P pauses and resumes.
- R starts a new game.

Add `data-testid="restart-btn"` — a button that starts a new game: empty board, score 0,
lines 0, level 1, running.

Then verify that nothing we built in earlier steps has broken, and fix anything that has.

statement: Add keyboard controls and a restart button, then verify no earlier functionality broke.
